description: RE-SCOPED after the fz-k22.7-holistic SPIKE DISPROVED the original 'CallSiteSummary settles from a pre-widened snapshot' framing. FINDING: there is NO single widening cell -- ActivationKey.arrow is a precise interned snapshot per exact input tuple, and Types::union mints a NEW Ty id (never mutates in place), so the two closures sharing a generic HOF body land on SIBLING ActivationKeys (traced: Ty(82)/Ty(131)/Ty(113)), each with its own CORRECT single-or-multi-target CallSiteSummary. This is activation-identity FRAGMENTATION (coarse 'which body' conflated with precise per-call evidence), which is exactly fz-xqw (SpecKey/BodyKey split) territory. Concretely: fz-k22.3's arg-floor fix takes find+find_value past the demand crash (they reach a genuinely multi-target callsite), but all?/any? STILL crashes identically at a sibling activation (Ty(82)) whose CallSiteSummary is genuinely, correctly single-target -- so the multi-target floor does not and should not apply there; the crash cause is DIFFERENT and unrelated to target-counting. TASK: (1) diagnose why the correctly-single-target all?/any? sibling leaves a backend value unbound (a distinct demand/materialization bug from the find-family multi-target case); (2) determine whether the fix is the fz-xqw SpecKey/BodyKey split (shared-body dispatch identity carrying precise per-call evidence) rather than anything local to fz-k22 -- if so, this should ride fz-xqw, not be re-invented here. Related: fz-xqw, fz-k22.3, fz-hwn.
title: fz-k22: all?/any? crashes at a correctly-single-target sibling activation -- activation-identity fragmentation (sibling ActivationKeys), likely rides fz-xqw not a settle-race
